_doc: BIRTHS (Phase 044): pregnancy and birth, behind the births switch (physical_subsystems.births, off by default). The physical side only: conception in a recorded union, the due day, the work and food a pregnancy costs, the delivery and its risks through harm(), and the newborn's genealogy. Which union a resident forms, and whether a resident wants a child, belong to the resident's backend. Sources, none checked against the text in this session (every figure is APPROX unless stated): conception_per_year is a natural (non-contracepting) marital fertility schedule by age, the shape of Henry (1961), 'Some data on natural fertility', Eugenics Quarterly 8: 81-91, and Coale and Trussell (1974), 'Model fertility schedules', Population Index 40: 185-258, lowered for the English village with Wrigley and Schofield (1981), The Population History of England 1541-1871 (marital fertility and birth spacing), and Hajnal (1965), European marriage patterns in perspective. gestation_days: about 266 days from conception, 280 from the last menstrual period, the standard obstetric reckoning; 270 is the brief's figure. postpartum_block_days: a birth stops conception for about a year while the mother nurses (lactational amenorrhoea); a design figure consistent with Wrigley and Schofield's account of nursing and birth spacing (APPROX). stillbirth and maternal_death are order-of-magnitude figures for a pre-modern English parish (APPROX). infant_first_year_death is 1 minus INFANT_SURVIVAL in population/household_composition.json (Wrigley and Schofield 1981), and the self-test checks that they agree. midwife_factor scales the maternal and first-year risks when a midwife is in reach (APPROX, a design figure). pregnancy_food and pregnancy_load are design figures (APPROX): food need rises by pregnancy_food while pregnant, and work capacity falls by up to max_load over the last part of the term, starting at from_term of the way through the term. nursed_hunger is the hunger a day an infant takes while its mother lives in its household and feeds it (a design figure: a nursed infant is fed at the breast; an orphaned one needs food from others, which is Phase 045's care). fertile_age_min and fertile_age_max bound the ages at which a woman can conceive.
